tasks.prompt:
A retailer sells 1,000 non-refundable credits for $25 each. Based on its
historical pattern, it expects 8% of credits to expire unused and has
sufficient evidence that the expected breakage will not be subject to a
significant reversal. During the period, customers redeem 700 credits.
Assuming revenue is recognized proportionately with redemptions, calculate
cumulative revenue recognized, including breakage, at period end.

A pharmaceutical licensing company enters a deal with a biotech startup:
  - Upfront license fee: $2,000,000
  - Milestone payment: $500,000 if the product receives FDA approval by
    December 31, 2027
  - The product is currently in Phase II clinical trials; Phase II-to-Phase III
    transition probability historically ranges from 40% to 55%
  - If the milestone is achieved, there is no risk of significant reversal
  - If the milestone is included in revenue and the product fails to receive
    approval, the $500,000 would require a complete reversal

Determine whether the milestone payment should be included in the transaction
price, applying the constraint analysis required by ASC 606-10-32-11 through
32-15. Show your reasoning and calculate the constrained transaction price.

An equipment manufacturer sells a machine for $800,000 and offers a two-year
extended warranty for an additional $60,000. The machine has a 95% probability
of operating without defect for 18 months and a 70% probability of operating
without defect for the full 24 months. Under the warranty, the manufacturer
would be obligated to repair or replace the machine if a defect occurs.

Historical data shows:
  - 30% of machines develop defects between months 18-24
  - Repair costs average $180,000
  - Replacement costs average $400,000
  - The expected cost per warranty is $62,000

Explain how the warranty obligation should be recognized and whether the
variable consideration constraint applies to any portion of the warranty
revenue.

A construction firm enters a contract to build a data center:
  - Base contract price: $12,000,000
  - Performance incentive: $1,500,000 if project completes 30 days early
  - Liquidated damages: $1,500,000 if project completes 30 days late
  - Projected completion: 60 days ahead of schedule (70% probability)
  - Risk of delay: 10% probability of being 30+ days late
  - The firm applies the expected-value method

Determine the transaction price, applying constraint analysis to the variable
consideration components. Show the expected-value calculation and explain
which components are constrained.

A customer is invoiced $12,000 each month for services performed during that
same month. The invoice amount corresponds directly to the value transferred
to the customer for the month, and there are no material financing effects.
May the entity recognize revenue at the amount to which it has a right to
invoice? State the condition that must be met.

An ERP vendor enters a contract to deliver a system implementation for a
manufacturing client:
  - Phase 1 (months 1-6): System configuration and testing, $800,000
  - Phase 2 (months 7-12): Data migration and go-live support, $600,000
  - Total contract: $1,400,000 for two distinct services
  - Phase 1 has a standalone selling price of $750,000
  - Phase 2 has a standalone selling price of $650,000

Midway through Phase 1 (month 3), the client requests an additional scope of
custom integration work not covered by either phase, priced at $350,000
(standalone selling price $320,000).

Classify this contract modification and determine the accounting treatment.
Show which method applies and explain why.

A cloud software vendor has a 24-month SaaS subscription contract:
  - Original monthly fee: $25,000 ($600,000 total)
  - The vendor has recognized $200,000 through month 8
  - The standalone selling price for the remaining 16 months is $380,000

At month 8, the client and vendor agree to add 50 additional user licenses
to the existing subscription. The additional licenses are not distinct from
the original subscription — they increase the capacity of the same hosted
service and cannot be used independently.
  - Additional monthly fee for the 50 licenses: $8,000 per month for the
    remaining 16 months ($128,000 total)
  - Standalone selling price of the additional licenses: $10,000 per month
    ($160,000 total)

Classify this contract modification and determine the accounting treatment.
Show the transaction price allocation and remaining revenue recognition.

A staffing firm provides temporary placement services under a 12-month
contract:
  - Monthly billing: $100,000 for 10 temporary workers
  - After 6 months, $600,000 has been recognized as revenue
  - The remaining obligation is 6 months of placement services

At month 6, the parties agree to:
  (1) Reduce the rate to $85,000 per month for the remaining 6 months
      ($510,000 total for the remaining period)
  (2) Add 2 additional temporary workers at $12,000 per month each
      for the remaining 6 months ($144,000 total)

The additional workers are distinct services that the firm regularly sells
separately (standalone selling price $144,000 for 6 months).

Classify this modification. Show the cumulative catch-up or prospective
treatment and the revenue impact.

A SaaS vendor signs a contract providing (1) a one-year hosted subscription,
(2) implementation configuration that does not create a separate asset for
the customer, and (3) ten hours of customer training. The vendor regularly
sells the hosted subscription and training separately, but the configuration
significantly modifies the hosted service. Identify the distinct performance
obligations and briefly explain the conclusion.

A software company sells a perpetual software license and a two-year
stand-ready support service. The customer can benefit from the license on its
own, and the support service is separately sold. Identify the performance
obligations.

A vendor sells a license and implementation service together for a stated
transaction price of $120,000. The standalone selling price of the license is
$100,000 and the standalone selling price of implementation is $50,000.
Allocate the transaction price to each performance obligation using relative
standalone selling prices. Return amounts to the nearest cent.

A software vendor contracts with a customer for a one-year cloud platform
license with the following terms:
  - Guaranteed annual subscription fee: $250,000
  - Usage-based overage fee: $150 per active user-month above 500 users,
    billed quarterly in arrears
  - Historical usage: the customer averaged 342 active users per month over
    the past 12 months, with a minimum of 280 and a maximum of 410
  - The customer is expanding its workforce by approximately 15% over the
    contract term
  - The vendor applies the expected-value method for variable consideration
    under ASC 606-10-32-8

Determine the transaction price and explain how variable consideration is
estimated and whether the constraint applies.

A consulting firm delivers a fixed-fee implementation project with the
following structure:
  - Fixed fee: $500,000
  - Success bonus: $200,000 payable if the client achieves a $10 million
    annualized cost reduction within 18 months
  - The client's internal analysis estimates a 60% probability of achieving
    $8 million of the target but only 30% of achieving the full $10 million
  - Historical data from similar engagements shows success rates of 25-40%
  - If the bonus is included and the client does not achieve the target, there
    is a moderate risk of significant revenue reversal

Determine the appropriate variable consideration amount using the most-likely-
amount method. Explain whether the constraint under ASC 606-10-32-11 should
be applied and, if so, how much of the bonus should be constrained.

A healthcare SaaS vendor contracts to deliver a two-year electronic health
records platform subscription:
  - Base annual subscription: $300,000 per year
  - Variable data migration fee: $25 per patient record migrated, estimated at
    8,000 patient records
  - Migration estimates have ranged from 6,500 to 9,500 records across
    similar engagements
  - Migration fee is invoiced upon completion of migration milestones
  - The vendor uses the expected-value method for variable consideration

Calculate the transaction price and explain how each component is treated
under ASC 606.
